chunk_findings.detail: `_json_files` keeps only `[autonomy].files` values that begin with `json:`; `verify` then treats a descriptor with any other file value as having no files and returns `ok`. Given a descriptor with `autonomy.none=False`, `profiles={}`, and `files={".codex/config.toml": "toml:approval_policy"}`, `_json_files` returns `{}`, so `verify` returns `Verdict(state="ok", detail="launch flags: none")` without inspecting the documented TOML allowlist. If that allowlist is absent or incomplete, the agent will still prompt, but the doctor reports it as safe.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/permissions.py:_json_files

chunk_findings.detail: When an `[autonomy]` section exists but has neither JSON allowlist files nor launch flags, `verify` still returns `ok`. For example, with `h.autonomy = Autonomy(none=False, profiles={}, files={})`, `_json_files(h)` is empty, the flags string becomes `"none"`, and the returned state is `ok`. That means the pipeline treats the agent as “will not prompt” even though the profile documents no mechanism to suppress prompts, so an unattended run can stall on the first tool call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/permissions.py:verify

chunk_findings.detail: `generate` can raise `AttributeError` on a valid JSON settings file whose root is a non-dict, instead of the documented `ValueError` or a safe skip. If the declared settings file contains a non-empty JSON array such as `[{"a": 1}]`, `_missing` reports the needed entries missing because `_get` returns `None` for non-dicts; then `generate` calls `_put` on the list at `doc.setdefault(...)`, crashing. This breaks `generate`, `diff`, and `apply` for a file that parsed successfully.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/permissions.py:generate

chunk_findings.detail: `test_not_verified_is_not_a_finding` does not actually test an unverified descriptor. `_doctor(repo, "")` writes `DESC + ""`, and `DESC` contains a `[verified]` section with a date and sources. Therefore the descriptor passed to `harness_view` is verified, so this test exercises the verified-without-autonomy path, not the unverified path implied by its name. If a regression causes `harness doctor` to emit permission findings for descriptors lacking `[verified]`, this test would still pass because it never creates such a descriptor.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_permissions_doctor.py:39

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_file_that_cannot_be_parsed_is_left_alone` asserts that a descriptor with an `[autonomy]` allowlist file whose JSON is malformed yields `state == "unverified"`. Given the declared `FILES` profile and a `.acme/settings.json` containing `{not json`, the pipeline sees an unverified state, and the companion doctor test (`test_not_verified_is_not_a_finding`) treats unverified as not a finding; therefore a corrupt permission allowlist is silently ignored and the unattended run can still stall when the agent fails to obtain the required permissions. This input should be reported as a concrete verification failure (e.g. `incomplete`/`stalls`/an error state), not as unverified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_permission_profiles.py:82

chunk_findings.detail: `generate` calls `_missing(repo, h)` which checks `_json_files(h)`, but if `_missing(repo, h)` returns a string (indicating an unreadable file error), the `isinstance(lack, str)` check raises `ValueError(lack)` *after* iterating over `lack.items()`. Wait, `isinstance(lack, str)` is checked before the loop in `generate`, but inside `_missing`, if `_read` returns an `Unreadable`, it returns a string. However, if `_read` returns `None` (file absent), `_missing` creates a dictionary where the missing entries are all entries, and `generate` proceeds to read `path.read_text()` which raises `FileNotFoundError` because `path` does not exist when the settings file is absent and needs to be created. Given input where a declared settings file in `[autonomy].files` does not yet exist on disk, `generate` will raise an unhandled `FileNotFoundError` at line 133 (`path.read_text()`), crashing the process when attempting to generate a fresh settings file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services.permissions:120

chunk_findings.detail: Given an autonomy section with `none` false, `profiles` empty, and no `json:` files, `verify` returns state `ok` and detail `launch flags: none`. Nothing disables prompts, so the agent still asks on every tool call and stalls the pipeline, but callers treat `ok` as safe to run unattended. The same false `ok` happens when `wanted()` is empty (family not in `ALLOW`) and a `json:` file is present: `_missing` finds no lacking entries and reports that the allowlist holds every entry ddflow needs, which is a guess, not a check.
chunk_findings.title: verify

chunk_findings.detail: Given settings `{"permissions": {"allow": ["Bash(git *)"], "deny": ["Bash(rm *)"]}}` and a descriptor key `json:permissions`, `_get` sees a dict, `_missing` treats that as an empty list, and `_put` replaces the object with a flat allow list. The `deny` rules are dropped, so the written file widens the agent past the narrowest allowlist even though only missing allow entries were supposed to be added. A non-list leaf should fail closed the way an unreadable file does, not be overwritten.
chunk_findings.title: generate

chunk_findings.detail: For any descriptor family that is not present in `ALLOW`, `wanted(h)` returns `()`. If such a descriptor has an `[autonomy].files` entry of the form `json:<key>`, `_json_files(h)` is non-empty, so `verify()` calls `_missing()`, which computes no missing entries because `need` is empty, and then returns `state="ok"` with “the allowlist holds every entry ddflow needs”. For example, with `h.family="codex"`, `h.autonomy.files={"config.json": "json:permissions.allow"}`, and `h.autonomy.profiles={}`, `verify()` says the agent will not prompt even though ddflow has no allowlist syntax for Codex and cannot know whether the file contains the entries needed to avoid prompts. The module’s stated contract is to answer “without ever guessing”; this path guesses `ok` instead of `unverified`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/permissions.py:verify

chunk_findings.detail: `_json_files()` silently ignores every `files` value that does not begin with `json:`. If a descriptor declares a file-based allowlist in another format and has no launch flags, `verify()` treats it as if there are no file-based entries and returns `ok`. For example, with `h.autonomy.files={"settings.toml": "toml:permissions.allow"}` and `h.autonomy.profiles={}`, `_json_files()` returns `{}`, so `verify()` returns `state="ok"` and detail “launch flags: none” without ever inspecting the declared allowlist. That can mark an agent as safe when the actual allowlist is missing or incomplete, causing the pipeline to stall.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/permissions.py:_json_files

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts that a present but unparseable allowlist is classified as `unverified`. That is wrong for this state: `unverified` is also used for a descriptor with no `[autonomy]` block (line 33), but here the operator has configured an autonomy file and it cannot be read. Given `.acme/settings.json` containing `{not json`, `P.verify(...)` returns `state == "unverified"`. Because the companion doctor test `test_not_verified_is_not_a_finding` says unverified verdicts are not findings, a corrupt permission profile is silently ignored instead of being reported as incomplete/invalid; the pipeline can then proceed and stall on prompts. The safe classification is `incomplete` (or an explicit invalid-config finding), because the wanted allowlist entries cannot be shown to be present.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_permission_profiles.py:74

chunk_findings.detail: `verify` treats an empty `wanted()` result as a complete allowlist. `ALLOW` only defines entries for `claude-code`, and `wanted` returns `()` for every other family. `_missing` then builds `lack` by filtering that empty tuple, so the dict is always `{}` and `verify` returns `state="ok"` with “the allowlist holds every entry ddflow needs”. Given family `gemini` (or kilo/codex/cursor), `[autonomy].none` false, `files={"settings.json": "json:permissions.allow"}`, and a missing or `[]` settings file, the agent still prompts on every tool call and the pipeline stalls, but the verdict is `ok` rather than `unverified`/`incomplete`. That is the opposite of “without ever guessing”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/permissions.py:124

chunk_findings.detail: When `[autonomy]` exists, `none` is false, and no `json:` files are declared, `verify` returns `ok` even if `profiles` is empty (`flags` becomes `"none"`). Given `autonomy.profiles={}`, `autonomy.files={}`, `autonomy.none=False`, family `claude-code`, the verdict is `ok` / `launch flags: none` while `ALLOW["claude-code"]` is unenforced, so the agent prompts and an unattended pipeline stalls with no `incomplete` or `stalls` finding.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/permissions.py:117

chunk_findings.detail: `generate` assumes the parsed settings root is a dict. `verify`/`_missing` treat a non-dict JSON root as an empty list (`_get` returns `None`), so a file whose contents are `[]` is reported `incomplete`. `generate` then does `doc = _read(...)` (the list) and `_put` calls `setdefault` on it, raising `AttributeError` instead of the documented `ValueError`. The operator cannot obtain the diff that `incomplete` says to apply.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/permissions.py:143
